strings.name: Ian McEwan
strings.summary: McEwan began with unsettling short fiction and developed precise narratives of ordinary people's moral choices. Amsterdam won the Booker Prize; Atonement joined memory, war and the responsibilities of writing. Science, law and technology also enter his characters' relationships. What We Can Know looks back from the future and asks how much we can know about others.

strings.timeline.t3.title: Published Machines Like Me
strings.timeline.t3.text: Used an alternative 1980s Britain and an artificial person to examine moral judgment.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Published Atonement
strings.timeline.t4.text: A family misunderstanding opens a story of war and memory, later widely adapted.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Won the Booker Prize
strings.timeline.t5.text: Amsterdam won for its story of friendship and a moral pact.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Published The Child in Time
strings.timeline.t6.text: Explored time, grief and public life through a missing child and parental experience; won the Whitbread award.
strings.timeline.t7.title: First story collection
strings.timeline.t7.text: First Love, Last Rites established his early style and won the Somerset Maugham Award the following year.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completed his literature degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: Graduated from Sussex before further literary training at East Anglia.
